330189.title: Garaschuk's conjecture on fractional triangle decompositions
330189.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices and minimum degree at least $\frac{3}{4}n$. **Garaschuk's conjecture.** If $n$ is large enough, then $G$ is fractionally $K_3$-decomposable. Fractional triangle decomposability is a relaxation of an actual triangle decomposition, and this conjecture would provide the fractional decomposition threshold needed in approaches to Nash-Williams' conjecture. The source presents it as a conjecture and identifies Garaschuk's result as the best known result towards Nash-Williams' conjecture, so its resolution status should be checked against the cited work.

330192.title: Nešetřil–Ossona de Mendez conjecture on bounded tree-depth components in 3-colorings of planar graphs
330192.literal_statement:
A **monochromatic component** is a connected component induced by vertices receiving the same color in a vertex coloring. The **tree-depth** of a graph is the minimum height of a rooted forest whose closure contains the graph.

**Nešetřil–Ossona de Mendez conjecture.** There exists a constant $t$ such that every planar graph has a vertex coloring with 3 colors in which every monochromatic component has tree-depth at most $t$.

The conjecture is refuted: the construction of $G_3$ in the paper gives planar graphs for which every 3-coloring has a monochromatic component containing a path of arbitrarily large length, and hence of arbitrarily large tree-depth.

330202.title: Path-factor existence conjecture for graphs without small odd paths
330202.literal_statement:
Let $k\geq 3$, and let $G$ be a graph. For a graph $H$, let $\mathcal{C}(H)$ be the set of components of $H$; for $i\geq 1$, let $\mathcal{C}_i(H)=\{C\in\mathcal{C}(H)\mid |V(C)|=i\}$ and let $c_i(H)=|\mathcal{C}_i(H)|$. A **$\{P_2,P_{2k+1}\}$-factor** is a spanning subgraph whose components are copies of $P_2$ or $P_{2k+1}$. **Path-factor existence conjecture.** If

$$
\sum_{0\leq i\leq k-1}c_{2i+1}(G-X)\leq \frac{4k+6}{8k+3}|X|
$$

for all $X\subseteq V(G)$, then $G$ has a $\{P_2,P_{2k+1}\}$-factor. The conjecture extends the corresponding sufficient conditions known for $k=1$ and $k=2$. For $k\geq 3$ divisible by $3$, examples show that the analogous bound with an additional constant term cannot guarantee such a factor, while the conjecture proposes that removing this constant term suffices in every case.
330202.mathematics: Must control every vertex deletion and construct a spanning P2/P(2k+1) factor for every k>=3. No dual factor obstruction satisfying all inequalities obtained; ordinary matching existence alone does not supply the permitted path lengths.

330262.title: The bounded-degree transversal conjecture for uniform hypergraphs
330262.literal_statement:
Let $k\ge 2$, and let $H$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges. Write $\tau(H)$ for its transversal number and $\Delta(H)$ for its maximum degree. **The bounded-degree transversal conjecture.** If $\Delta(H)\le 3$, then

$$
\tau(H)\le \frac{n}{k}+\frac{m}{6}.
$$

The conjecture extends the known cases for $k=2,3$ and addresses the remaining bounded-degree case; the paper notes that the corresponding inequality can fail when $k\ge 4$ and $\Delta(H)\ge 4$.

330263.title: The linear 4-uniform hypergraph transversal conjecture
330263.literal_statement:
Let $H$ be a $4$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges. Recall that $H$ is **linear** if every two edges intersect in at most one vertex, and let $\tau(H)$ denote its transversal number. **The linear transversal conjecture.** If $H$ is linear, then

$$
\tau(H)\le \frac{n}{4}+\frac{m}{6}.
$$

The paper presents this as a proposed extension of its bounded-degree result. It is motivated by the failure of the same bound for some hypergraphs of maximum degree at least $4$, while linearity rules out repeated intersections between pairs of edges.

330264.title: The spectral characterization of geodesic growth for right-angled Coxeter groups on trees
330264.literal_statement: Let $T$ and $T'$ be trees. Assume that they are simultaneously co-spectral, their complements are co-spectral, and their line graphs are co-spectral. **Geodesic-growth conjecture.** Then $T$ and $T'$ have the same geodesic growth, meaning that the associated right-angled Coxeter groups $G(T)$ and $G(T')$ have the same geodesic growth series. The conjecture asks whether these three spectral data determine geodesic growth for right-angled Coxeter groups based on trees; the paper establishes examples supporting the question but does not resolve the general implication.

330276.title: Non-polynomial growth for k-dominating independent sets in incidence graphs of projective planes
330276.literal_statement:

330301.title: Classification conjecture for admissible anti-automorphisms of affine Hecke algebras
330301.literal_statement:
Let ${\mathcal H}$ be the affine Hecke algebra, with parameter ${\mathbf q}$, extended torus ${\mathcal T}$, and elements $\theta_x$ for $x\in X$. An automorphism $\kappa$ of ${\mathcal H}$ is **admissible** if it fixes ${\mathbf q}$ and each $T_w$, and satisfies $\kappa({\mathcal I}_a)\subseteq {\mathcal I}_{\hat\kappa(a)}$ for every $a\in{\mathcal T}$; here $\hat\kappa:{\mathcal T}\times{\mathbb C}^{\times}\to{\mathcal T}\times{\mathbb C}^{\times}$ is the induced map on the spectrum of the center. The operations $\bullet$ and $\star$ are admissible.

**Classification conjecture.** If $\kappa$ is an admissible involutive anti-automorphism, then:

1. If $\hat\kappa(a)=a$ for all $a\in{\mathcal T}$, then
 
$$
\kappa(\theta_x)=\theta_x^\bullet
$$

 for all $x\in X$.
2. If $\hat\kappa(a)=a^{-1}$ for all $a\in{\mathcal T}$, then
 
$$
\kappa(\theta_x)=\theta_x^\star
$$

 for all $x\in X$.

The conjecture proposes that the action of an admissible involutive anti-automorphism on the Bernstein elements $\theta_x$ is determined by its induced action on the torus: the identity action gives the $\bullet$ operation, while inversion gives the $\star$ operation. It is motivated by the corresponding classification for graded affine Hecke algebras and the relationship between affine and graded Hecke algebras.
330301.mathematics: Admissibility includes preservation of central fibers, not merely fixing Bernstein generators or the finite Hecke subalgebra. No nonstandard involution satisfying all fiber conditions constructed.

330343.title: Field-extension conjecture for square roots of cyclotomic units
330343.literal_statement:
Let $czeta_k$ and $czeta_m$ be primitive roots of unity. **Field-extension conjecture.**

$$
\sqrt{1+4\zeta_k}\in\mathbb Q\left(\zeta_m\right)\Longleftrightarrow k=1\text{ and }5\mid m\text{ or }k=2\text{ and }3\mid m.
$$

Only the implication from left to right is open; the reverse implication is established in the paper. The conjecture characterizes when the relevant quadratic extension is already contained in a cyclotomic field and is used to determine convergence behavior of the generalized Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction at roots of unity.

330460.title: The winding-number-zero extinction-time conjecture for curve diffusion flow
330460.literal_statement:
Let a curve diffusion flow start from a smooth immersed curve with winding number zero, and let its initial length be $L$. Let $T_{\mathrm{flow}}$ denote its maximal existence time, and let $T_{\mathrm{eight}}(L)$ denote the existence time of a self-similarly shrinking figure eight with initial length $L$. **Extinction-time conjecture.** The maximal existence time satisfies

$$
T_{\mathrm{flow}}\leq T_{\mathrm{eight}}(L).
$$

The conjecture proposes that the self-similar figure eight gives the largest possible existence time among flows starting from curves with winding number zero; the source presents this as a heuristic motivated by the generic development of curvature singularities, but gives no resolution.

330471.title: Dvořák's conjecture on coloring squares of girth-five planar graphs
330471.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph with girth $5$, let $\Delta$ denote its maximum degree, and let $M$ be a constant. The **Dvořák conjecture.** There exists some constant $M$ such that every planar graph $G$ with girth $5$ and maximum degree at least $M$ satisfies

$$
\Delta(G^2)\le\Delta+2.
$$

Here $G^2$ is the square of $G$ and $\Delta(G^2)$ denotes its maximum degree. This conjecture concerns the remaining high-degree, girth-five case after known results for larger girth; the supplied text gives no resolution, so it is open.

330502.title: The age conjecture for counting G-fields
330502.literal_statement:
Let $K$ be a number field, let $G$ be a finite group, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional faithful representation of $G$ over $K$. Let $N_{G,V,K}(B)$ count isomorphism classes of $G$-fields $L/K$ with $V$-discriminant $D_L^V\le B$. Let $\operatorname{age}(G)$ be the minimum of the age function on $G\setminus\{1\}$, and let $\upsilon(G)$ be the number of nontrivial $K$-conjugacy classes with minimum age. **The age conjecture.** If $K$ is sufficiently large, then 
$$
N_{G,V,K}(B)\sim CB^{1/\operatorname{age}(G)}(\log B)^{\upsilon(G)}.
$$
 This is proposed as a representation-theoretic analogue of Malle's conjecture, with age replacing index; the source gives no resolution status.

330504.title: The generalized Malle conjecture for linear group actions
330504.literal_statement:
Let $K$ be a number field and let $G$ act faithfully and linearly on $V=\mathbb{A}_K^d$, with the associated map $\overline{V}\to\overline{X}=\overline{V}/G$ étale in codimension one. Let $N(G,V,B)$ count $G$-fields with extended $V$-discriminant at most $B$, and let $\operatorname{age}(G)$ be the minimum age of a nontrivial element of $G$. Let $\upsilon(G)$ be the number of youngest $K$-conjugacy classes. **The generalized Malle conjecture.** If $K$ is sufficiently large, then 
$$
N(G,V,B)\sim CB^{1/\operatorname{age}(G)}(\log B)^{\upsilon(G)-1}.
$$
 This extends Malle's predicted exponent from permutation representations to general faithful linear actions; the source gives no resolution status.

330507.title: Chen–Dehmer–Shi's extremal entropy conjecture for trees
330507.literal_statement:
Let $T$ be a tree with $n$ vertices. Let $S_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor,\lceil n/2\rceil}$ be the balanced double star, and let $CS(n,t)$ denote a comet; write $t_0$ for the parameter specified by the conjecture. The entropy under consideration is $I_{f^n_2}$.

**Chen–Dehmer–Shi's conjecture.** The balanced double star and the comet $CS(n,t_0)$ attain the maximum and minimum values of $I_{f^n_2}(T)$, respectively.

The conjecture is motivated by the preceding comparison between the star, path and balanced double star and by the proposed extremal role of the comet. The source does not provide a proof or a resolution.

330599.title: Exact-value conjecture for the multi-nut caching game
330599.literal_statement:
Consider the caching game with $k=j\ge2$, where the hider caches $k$ nuts, the searcher aims to find all $k$, and the parameters include $n$ holes and search depth $h$. The source proves the upper bound

$$
\text{value}\le\frac{h^k}{{n+k-1\choose k}}.
$$

**Multi-nut exact-value conjecture.** If

$$
k=j\ge2,\qquad\frac{k+1}{k-1}\le h\le\frac nk,
$$

then the value of the game is

$$
\frac{h^k}{{n+k-1\choose k}}.
$$

The conjecture extends the two-nut analysis; the source suggests that the integral-depth case may be easier but does not prove the full statement.

330624.title: Diadem–nucleus characterization of König–Egerváry graphs
330624.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $
u(G)$ denote its maximum matching size, and let $\alpha(G)$ denote its independence number. Write $\mathrm{diadem}(G)$ for the union of all critical independent sets of $G$, and $\mathrm{nucleus}(G)$ for their intersection.

**Diadem–nucleus conjecture.** If

$$
\left\vert \mathrm{diadem}(G)\right\vert +\left\vert \mathrm{nucleus}(G)\right\vert =2\alpha(G),
$$

then $G$ is a König–Egerváry graph, that is, $\left\vert V(G)\right\vert=\alpha(G)+\nu(G)$.

This proposes a sufficient condition for a graph to be König–Egerváry, linking the union and intersection of its critical independent sets to its independence number. The supplied text does not indicate whether the problem has been resolved.

330674.title: Strong diameter conjecture for direct powers of finite groups
330674.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $G^n$ denote its $n$-th direct power, and let $D(G^n)$ denote the diameter with respect to a generating set, using words in that set. Write ${\mathrm{rank}}(G)$ for the minimum size of a generating set of $G$. **Strong diameter conjecture.** The diameter $D(G^n)$ is at most

$$
n\bigl(|G|-{\mathrm{rank}}(G)\bigr).
$$

The bound would give a linear, rather than exponential, estimate in $n$ for direct powers; it is proposed as a stronger form of the accompanying assertion concerning a suitable minimum generating set.

330675.title: Weak diameter conjecture for direct powers of finite groups
330675.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $G^n$ denote its $n$-th direct power, and let $A$ be a generating set of minimum size for $G^n$. Write ${\mathrm{rank}}(G)$ for the minimum size of a generating set of $G$, and let ${\mathrm{diam}}(G^n,A)$ be the diameter with respect to $A$. **Weak diameter conjecture.** There exists a generating set $A$ for $G^n$ of minimum size such that

$$
{\mathrm{diam}}(G^n,A)\leq n\bigl(|G|-{\mathrm{rank}}(G)\bigr).
$$

This is the weaker companion to the assertion for the diameter with respect to any generating set, and is intended to provide a polynomial bound for the diameter of direct powers.

330762.title: Lawson–Simons conjecture for submanifolds in spheres
330762.literal_statement:
Let $F_{0}:M^{n}\to\mathbb{S}^{n+q}$ be an $n$-dimensional closed submanifold satisfying

$$
|h|^{2}<2\sqrt{n-1},
$$

where $h$ is the second fundamental form. **Lawson–Simons conjecture.** The mean curvature flow with initial value $F_{0}$ converges to a round point or a totally geodesic sphere. 330764.title: The extremal number conjecture for powers of balanced rooted trees
330764.literal_statement:
Let $(T,R)$ be a balanced rooted tree, let $T^p$ be the graph formed from the union of $p$ distinct labelled copies of $T$ that agree on the roots $R$ and are otherwise disjoint, and let $\rho_T$ denote the rooted density of $T$. **Extremal number conjecture.** For any balanced rooted tree $(T,R)$,

330804.title: EKR conjecture for depth-two claws
330804.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a depth-two claw with $n$ leaves. For a positive integer $r$, let $G$ be $r$-EKR when no pairwise intersecting family of independent sets of size $r$ in $G$ is larger than the largest $r$-star, where an $r$-star is the family of such sets containing a fixed vertex.

**Depth-two-claw EKR conjecture.** Let $n$ and $r$ be positive integers, with $n > r$, and let $G$ be a depth-two claw with $n$ leaves. Then $G$ is $r$-EKR.

The conjecture is motivated by the construction of a non-star intersecting family showing that the boundary case $r=n$ fails, together with the paper's theorem for related depth-two claw cases. Its general status is left open in the source.

330820.title: Odlyzko–Stanley conjecture on the growth of $p$-Stanley sequences
330820.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime. A **$p$-Stanley sequence** $S_p(A)=a_1,a_2,\ldots$ is generated greedily from a $p$-free set $A$ of nonnegative integers, by adjoining at each step the smallest larger integer that preserves $p$-freeness. **Odlyzko–Stanley conjecture.** Every $p$-Stanley sequence satisfies one of the following two growth laws:

$$
a_n=\Theta\left(n^{\log_{p-1}p}\right)
$$

or

$$
a_n=\Theta\left(\frac{n^{(p-1)/(p-2)}}{(\log n)^{1/(p-2)}}\right).
$$

The first law is the modular, digit-structured behavior, while the second is the conjectured chaotic behavior motivated by the authors' heuristic. The source gives no resolution of this conjecture.

330908.title: The minimum-degree conjecture for distance-preserving graphs
330908.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum degree. A graph is **distance preserving** if it has an isometric subgraph of every order from $1$ to $n$.

$$
\delta(G)>n/2,
$$

then $G$ is distance preserving.

330947.title: Uniqueness conjecture for the minimising matrix of $c_n$
330947.literal_statement:
Let $K_n$ be the set of all $n\times n$ lower triangular $(0,1)$-matrices with every diagonal entry equal to $1$, and let $c_n$ be the minimum of the smallest eigenvalues of $YY^T$ over $Y\in K_n$. For each $n\geq2$, let $Y_0\in K_n$ be the matrix with entries

$$
(Y_0)_{ij}=\begin{cases}0&\text{if }i<j,\\1&\text{if }i=j,\\frac{1-(-1)^{i+j}}{2}&\text{if }i>j.\end{cases}
$$

**Uniqueness conjecture.** There is a unique matrix $Y\in K_n$ such that the smallest eigenvalue of $YY^T$ is $c_n$. Equivalently, if the smallest eigenvalue of $YY^T$ equals $c_n$, then $Y=Y_0$.

The authors report finding no matrix other than $Y_0$ with this property for $n=2,3,\ldots,9$. The conjecture strengthens the preceding minimisation claim by asserting uniqueness, but the supplied text gives no resolution.

331134.title: Prime Coxeter number conjecture for dominant numbers of dual fundamental series

Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be the simple Lie algebra considered in the topological ODE construction, with Coxeter number $h$, rank $n$, and dual fundamental series $\phi_{a;a}$ for $a\in\{1,\dots,n\}$.
